title: Sound for AI-made edits (Openverse, Real SFX, earshot)
creator: Unnamed Instagram creator
one_liner: An edit without sound effects feels like a silent movie; give every visual event a real sound.
why_it_matters: Your Khandala and incline edits went out silent, with music added later. Sound is half of what makes a reel feel 'pro', and it's the part an AI editor skips because it can't hear. This reel names a free three-part stack (a sound library, a placer and 'ears') that fixes exactly that gap.

big_idea.statement: AI edits look pro but sound empty; fix it with a library of real sounds, a tool that places them on the exact frame, and a tool that listens back.
support: An AI editing agent can't hear, so it skips sound or fakes it with synthetic beeps.
Openverse gives millions of openly licensed sounds, searchable with no API key.
Real SFX finds the moments that need sound and places real recordings on that frame.
earshot lets the agent listen: it scores a mix against pro launch films and can make whooshes in code.
Admitting a tool's limit ('only 78 sounds') makes the rest believable.

chapters.title: The three-part sound stack
chapters.summary: The fix is three tools, each with one job. A source library: Openverse, a free search over millions of openly licensed sounds with no API key. Placement: Real SFX, a Claude Code skill that finds every moment in an edit that needs sound and places a real recording on that frame. Ears: earshot, an open-source tool that lets the agent listen, scoring an edit against pro launch films and generating its own whooshes in code. The creator is upfront that Real SFX only ships 78 UI sounds, which is why you pair it with a library.

chapters.title: What the tools really are
chapters.summary: Each tool was checked on its own site or repo. Openverse is a search API over CC-licensed audio (mostly from Freesound), free and keyless, but every sound carries its own licence: use CC0 for Instagram, and credit CC-BY sounds in the caption. A test search for 'whoosh' returned 240 results. Real SFX needs Python 3.9+ and ffmpeg, places sounds from your own folder, and outputs an MP4, an SFX WAV and a report. earshot is an MIT-licensed CLI and MCP server with commands like critique, timeline, forge and sfx; it downloads about 1.1 GB of models on first run.

chapters.title: How the reel is built
chapters.summary: In 42 seconds the reel goes problem, three numbered tools, a summary card, then the CTA. Something changes every 1.5–2.5 seconds: n/3 badges, slide-in cards and animated number counters (5,220,123 sounds; GitHub stars ticking up). Emphasis words like 'pro' and 'honest' are set in serif italic over a clean sans body, with yellow and orange keyword highlights. Frosted UI cards spring in with a bounce. And it practises its own message: a pop, click, whoosh or snap lands on every visual change.

chapters.title: The CTA and what it means for us
chapters.summary: The reel ends on 'Comment SOUND and I'll send you all three links' with an animated comment badge. For our pipeline this is the exact gap: ffmpeg can measure loudness and levels but can't judge how a mix sounds, and our reels went out silent. With CC0 sounds from Openverse, Real SFX-style placement and an earshot critique, we can add pops on text, whooshes on cuts and a thud on the final lockout ourselves, then check the mix before you add the song in Edits.

glossary.def: Sound effects: short sounds (pop, whoosh, thud) placed on visual events.

try_it.title: Sound pass on an old gym reel
steps: Open your last silent gym edit.
List every visual event (cut, text pop, counter tick, final rep).
Find CC0 sounds on Openverse: pop, whoosh, thud, chime.
Place one sound per event, quieter than your voice.
Add the song last, well under the SFX.

try_it.title: Contrast hook for a PC reel
steps: Write 'Looks ___. Runs/sounds like ___.' for your PC.
Film the 'looks' shot (RGB, clean case) and the 'runs like' proof (stutter, fan noise).
Cut them back to back in the first 3 s with a hard stop in the sound.

try_it.title: n/3 badge gaming list
steps: Pick three settings that improved your game.
Give each a 1/3, 2/3, 3/3 badge that springs in with a pop.
Add a number counter for the before/after stat (FPS, K/D).
End with 'the honest part:' and one limitation.
